title: Vacances
identity: Jean-Michel Damase, Vacances, Billaudot GB4949 (1990), for E-flat alto saxophone and piano, approximately three minutes. The publisher lists “Facile (cycle 1)” and adults as audience; the French Wind Music Archive describes a preparatory level indicated on the score. A University of Panama recital project reproduces selected excerpts attributed to this edition and discusses it in an undergraduate recital context.

evidence.claim: Publisher product page identifies GB4949 as E-flat saxophone and piano, c. 3 minutes, copyright 1990, “Facile (cycle 1),” and adult audience.

French Wind Music Archive catalog identifies the 1990 Billaudot edition for alto saxophone in E-flat and piano, 3+1 pages, with “niveau préparatoire indiqué sur la partition”; this is the archive’s bibliographic description and does not establish the complete part’s demands.

A University of Panama undergraduate recital-project PDF reproduces score excerpts attributed to the 1990 Gérard Billaudot edition, and I visually inspected its opening, syncopation, high-register, and closing excerpts (printed pp. 7, 9–10). These are excerpts, not the complete score.
evidence.source_name: University of Panama recital project with score excerpts

score_observations: The university project’s reproduced opening excerpt shows 12/8 and Moderato with dotted quarter = 76; the saxophone rests through several opening beats before a slurred melodic figure. Visually inspected later excerpts show syncopation, a high-register phrase with leaps and a rapid connected descent, and an active closing figure with short rests. These are selected excerpts copied from the 1990 Billaudot edition, not a full score; exact written range was not verified.
review_focus: The inspected excerpts suggest attention to pulse in 12/8, syncopated articulation, high-register connections, and phrase shaping; the complete part remains unseen.
collection_flag: Original saxophone/piano work. Publisher audience metadata says adults and “Facile (cycle 1)”; the archive describes preparatory-level notation. An undergraduate recital project also documents student use. These are different contexts, not a college-year mapping.

score_links.description: University project PDF with reproduced excerpts credited to the 1990 Billaudot edition; selected score excerpts visually inspected, not a complete score.
Opened publisher page confirms edition metadata; page does not show score notation.

gaps: Only selected score excerpts reproduced in the university project were available, not the complete Billaudot part; full written range and later demands remain unknown.
No matching professional recording or specific conservatory placement was verified.
